clue.text: He wrote "more law reforms"

indicators.note: reforms says the letters of the quoted phrase are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer is credited with a campaign slogan calling for more legal reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'more law' look like a slogan; it is the fodder, and 'reforms' rearranges its letters into the Elizabethan dramatist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan playwright, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: Being thought about is not being well-treated

indicators.note: about means around, so the thought word goes around the other

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Being pondered over feels like being handled badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated wrongly or abused is the opposite of being handled well.

clue.text: Debauched guy made to carry the can as usual

indicators.note: being made to carry something means holding it inside

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A dissolute man is blamed for something, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry the can' is an idiom for taking the blame; here it splits into a container indicator and its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regular and habitual is the ordinary, usual way.

clue.text: Issue of note — bound to be

parts.note: taken as written
F is a musical note
a spring is a bound or leap

explanation.surface: A matter of importance that is sure to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter or problem but means children; 'of note' looks like a phrase meaning important.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or descendants are a person's issue in legal language.

clue.text: Time may be pressing

explanation.surface: Time might be running short and urgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' suggests urgency, but it means flattening, making things level, as with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day after afternoon is a time; making things level or flat is what pressing does.

clue.text: Wine is really essential to such a blissful dinner

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the run of words, essential to the phrase as part of its core

explanation.surface: A diner insists a certain white wine is a must for a perfect meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white wine from Burgundy in France is a named example of wine.

clue.text: Caught and beat a six-footer for making a noise

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to lam is to beat or thrash
an ant is an insect with six legs, so a six-footer

explanation.surface: Someone caught a tall person and thrashed him for being loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect, which has six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means loud and insistent, clamouring, so noisy.

clue.text: A woman holds it to show good-will

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one word goes inside the woman's name

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman holds something out as a sign of friendliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly relations, peace and friendship, amount to goodwill.

clue.text: Feel a little uncertain about silver and green stuff

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the symbol for silver
a little uncertain means not settled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone feels unsure about silver and greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little uncertain' makes LEAFE from FEEL A, and 'about' wraps that round AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage, the leaves of plants collectively, is green stuff.

clue.text: States small change in school appears questionable

indicators.note: in puts the states and the small change inside the school

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought
US is the United States
P stands for penny, small change

explanation.surface: Small change in a school appears doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful or dubious, open to suspicion, is questionable.

clue.text: Appear evasive when there's a deal to be made?

definitions.text: when there's a deal to be made?

explanation.surface: Someone dodges questions just as an important deal is about to be struck.
explanation.definitionFit: To be evasive is to dodge or prevaricate, a sense of the verb; and cards are mixed up before a card game's deal.

clue.text: The beasts, to strike in a recession!

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to slam is to strike hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the brutes will hit out during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks like an economic downturn, but it means a going back: the indicator turns the whole of 'to strike in a' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals is the plural general word for beasts, creatures of the non-human kind.

clue.text: Save to get married in spring

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for married inside the word for spring

parts.note: to skip is to spring or leap lightly

explanation.surface: Advice to economise ahead of a spring wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is the verb meaning to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise or stint, using as little as possible, is a sense of this verb.

clue.text: No matter what is packed by no matter whom?

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what gets packed regardless of who does the packing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: something packed by anyone at all ends up in somebody's case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless or whatever happens; read literally it is inside a case belonging to anyone at all.

clue.text: Having a lean period?

parts.note: a lean period sounds like hard times, but here it is a spell of eating little to become lean

explanation.surface: Someone going through a financially thin patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricting food intake to slim down is a time of getting leaner.

clue.text: Ill-fitting set sent tight as can be

indicators.note: ill-fitting means put together badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A set of clothes was delivered that turned out very tight.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of tense, most taut or stretched, matches tightest.

clue.text: An individual without equal. That could be put no plainer!

indicators.note: could be put suggests the letters can be placed in another order

explanation.surface: A matchless person, described as simply as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing having no match or rival; a paragon.

clue.text: Load borne by soldiers going into battle

indicators.note: going into puts the soldiers inside the word for battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps, so soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry heavy packs as they march into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne by' is a link here: the load is what is carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by lorry, ship or train make up a cargo or load.

clue.text: Delicate kid getting into line

indicators.note: getting into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a file is a line, as in single file
to kid is to tease, as is to rag

explanation.surface: A sensitive child joins a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child; it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily broken or weak, frail, is delicate.

clue.text: Once sat for a picture in the nude

parts.note: ex means once or formerly
posed means sat for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone once modelled for a painting without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncovered, laid bare, unclothed.

clue.text: Rows about the non-drinker raising laughs

indicators.note: about means around, so the rows go around the non-drinker

parts.note: tiers are rows or levels
TT is teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: Arguments about an abstainer cause amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels; it means tiers. 'raising' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous suppressed giggles, a kind of laughs.

clue.text: Form's study expedition

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a tour is a journey or expedition

explanation.surface: A school form goes on a study trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a school class; it means shape or outline.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or shape of something, as on a map's height lines, is its form.

clue.text: Case put badly but coming to the point

indicators.note: badly signals letters out of order

explanation.surface: An argument poorly made but eventually reaching its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending in a cusp, a sharp point, is tapering to a point.

clue.text: Excel in public work

parts.note: overt means open or public
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Doing well in work for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or rise above others is to excel.

clue.text: Regret having to do with code

parts.note: re means concerning, having to do with
Morse is a telegraph code

explanation.surface: Regret about a coded message.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow for wrongdoing is a feeling of regret.

clue.text: Muggins encompasses appropriate breathy sounds

indicators.note: encompasses means surrounds, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: muggins is a fool, an ass
to pirate is to appropriate or steal

explanation.surface: A fool takes in fitting puffs of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, these are sounds pronounced with a puff of breath, like the h sound.

clue.text: The right hand a person used for running water

parts.note: R stands for right
one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone right-handed was used for fetching water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhone is a river of Switzerland and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is flowing water.

clue.text: Set across a light

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: Something positioned across a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: At right angles to a ship's keel, on a line crosswise of the vessel.

clue.text: Horse in trouble near the coast

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and put into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse in difficulty close to the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to the shore, as opposed to out at sea.

clue.text: A superior party offering support

parts.note: something better is superior

explanation.surface: A political party claims to be the superior one offering support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is not political: it means a person, one who aids or encourages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who aids or encourages, usually a crime, supports it.

clue.text: Non-stop, totally without aim

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
less means without, as in a suffix

explanation.surface: Someone is going on and on with no purpose at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order to the clue: 'without aim' becomes the aim word followed by the word for without.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on for ever, without a break, is never stopping.

clue.text: Hide cuts in energy repeatedly

indicators.note: in places the cuts between the two energy symbols
repeatedly means the energy symbol is used twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
clips are cuts or snips

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about repeated reductions in power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure or block from view, as the moon does the sun, is to conceal.
